title: finding(agents): `os-dev` tells devs the PM has already claimed the issue and not to touch the assignee — both repos' CLAUDE.md require the dev to claim first, and three devs hit the contradiction in one morning
body:
Filed unassigned and unlabelled by the `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat (session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`), recording a measurement for triage to grade and route. Intended reader is the `domain:skills` seat — `.claude/agents/**` is its territory. ⛔ No `domain:*` or `type` applied here; that is triage's to produce.

## The contradiction

`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:46` tells every dispatched dev:

> 2. **issue 已由 PM 认领**(大家共享同一 GitHub 身份)。不要动 assignee;若发现与他人在途

That is: *the issue has already been claimed by the PM — do not touch the assignee.*

Both repos' `CLAUDE.md` say the opposite, as the **first** rule in the file:

> Assign the issue to yourself … as the **first action of the task** — before the worktree, before the first read. … a claim is assign **plus a claim comment with your session ID and branch**

## Why it bites in practice, rather than being a harmless overlap

This lane's dispatch protocol sets `pm:dispatched` and **deliberately leaves the assignee to the dev's own claim** — because all agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field cannot say *whose* claim it is, and the session ID in the claim comment is the only real evidence. **An unassigned card is therefore the expected state when a dev arrives**, which is exactly the state `os-dev.md:46` tells the dev cannot happen.

## Measured: three devs hit it in one morning

All three resolved it correctly and all three spent tokens on it, and each flagged it rather than silently picking a side:

- **objectui#6241** — "the issue was UNASSIGNED when this seat picked it up, so the os-dev standing clause 'the PM has already claimed it, do not touch the assignee' did not hold"
- **objectui#6493** — "the os-dev contract says the PM has claimed the issue and I must not touch the assignee; the dispatch order and the repo CLAUDE.md both say to assign myself … I flag the conflict here rather than silently picking a side"
- **objectui#6488** — "the standing dev contract says not to touch the assignee, while this card's dispatch and objectui hygiene both said to claim first — the dispatch is per-card and more recent"

⚠️ **One of the three claimed LATE** — after its first edit rather than before it — and said so. That is the actual cost: the ambiguity does not just burn reasoning, it delays the claim, which is the window in which two agents can start the same card. That is the failure the claim-first rule exists to prevent.

## One executable criterion

`.claude/agents/os-dev.md` line 46's clause is either removed or qualified, such that a dev arriving at an **unassigned** issue with a `pm:dispatched` label reads an unambiguous instruction to assign itself and post a claim comment carrying its session ID and branch.

Whichever way it is written, the two documents must agree, because a dev that reads both today gets opposite instructions on its very first action.

## Not proposing the wording

Which document yields is a `domain:skills` call, not this seat's. Worth noting for whoever takes it: the clause is not simply wrong — it describes a PM protocol in which the PM *does* assign at dispatch, which may be how another seat runs. If seats legitimately differ, the fix is to make the clause conditional on what the dev observes rather than asserting a state, since the dev can always read the assignee and the comments and does not need to be told in advance.

## Evidence class

**Read from source and from three independent dev reports, not measured by a gate.** No gate exists that would catch two agent-facing documents disagreeing; that absence may itself be worth a thought when this is graded.
